assessments.reasoning: Event 4f2b91d3fd674c4282dcdd8e795c3cc2, Mozilla archive, NPL 1.0 governing revision 1, [19686,20248). Amendment IV supplies the exception. Amendment II defines Branded Code by authorized distribution under Netscape-controlled marks unlicensed under the NPL. No underlying contract was inspected.

challenge.method: Tested a later-acquired component, an ordinary downstream distributor, and an unrestricted component bundled alongside restricted code.
challenge.results: Each case lacks a stated condition. Amendment IV specifies the prior license, Netscape as actor and the extent of its contractual limitation. Mere third-party ownership is insufficient.

limitations: The third-party licensing must precede licensing the Original Code under this license. The exception concerns the reintegrated code, even if it would otherwise constitute Modifications.
reasoning: NPL 1.0 Amendment IV permits Netscape to reintegrate into Covered Code third-party code previously licensed for use in Netscape’s Branded Code. The source-distribution exception extends only as far as the contractual restriction on making that code available under the NPL.
